FAQ.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
FAQ.paragraph: We have answered the most common questions, related with registrations, please feel free to

questions_list.question: Do I need a subscription to become a member?
questions_list.answer: A subscription to IEEE is not mandatory to participate in our teams. However, members with a subscription enjoy significant benefits, such as priority access to events with limited spots and participation in official IEEE competitions, among many others. It's also important to note that by subscribing, you support the branch itself, as part of the funds return to us, which we can use for purchasing equipment and organizing events.

questions_list.question: Must I actively participate in a scientific group/project?
questions_list.answer: Our goal is to create an active community. For this reason, we encourage every member to be part of at least one team and actively participate in one of its projects. However, in cases where participation is temporarily not possible, this can be discussed with the respective team leader or project manager.

questions_list.question: Is any previous knowledge/experience required or can I learn through participating?
questions_list.answer: There are no prior knowledge requirements for joining the branch. However, it is up to the team leader/project manager to set any specific knowledge requirements to ensure the best organization of a project.

questions_list.question: How much time do I need to devote?
questions_list.answer: The time required depends on how many projects you participate in and the demands of each project. However, a few hours per week are usually sufficient.

questions_list.question: Do I need to be an electrical or electronics engineer in order to participate?
questions_list.answer: No! The branch is open to everyone, regardless of department. In addition to the scientific groups, there are many other teams that manage important aspects of the branch and relate to fields unrelated to engineering. You can get involved with these teams after discussing them through the registration form.

questions_list.question: Must you be a student to be a part of the branch?
questions_list.answer: No. Although most members are usually undergraduates, mostly due to more free time, there is no limit to who can participate in our teams or attend our events.

IEEE.title: What is the IEEE?
IEEE.caption: The world's largest technological organization
IEEE.text: The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) is the world's largest technical professional organization, focused on advancing technology for the benefit of humanity.
bulletedList: It was founded in 1963 through the merger of the American Institute of Electrical Engineers and the Institute of Radio Engineers.
The organization's headquarters are located in New York.
It is the largest organization of technology professionals, with approximately 430,000 members in around 160 countries.
The majority of members are engineers and scientists/academics. Most of them are computer scientists, software engineers, IT professionals, physicists, and even doctors.
For this reason, the organization often prefers using the acronym IEEE rather than its full name.

IEEEStudents.title: What is an IEEE Student Branch (SB)?
IEEEStudents.caption: University-based IEEE Community
IEEEStudents.text: An IEEE Student Branch (SB) is a branch of IEEE at universities. It is aimed at students in the same scientific fields as IEEE. The branch exists to connect students and professionals with each other within the same and across other universities or with industry professionals, in order to promote education and the technical development of electrical engineering, telecommunications, computer science, and unified standards. To achieve this, it organizes technical events and creates applications in this scientific field, which can be funded and promoted through IEEE. Student branches exist at universities around the world, including in Greece.
IEEEStudents.imageAlt: A random collection of greek IEEE SB logos

IEEEGreeceSection.title: What is the Greece Section?
IEEEGreeceSection.caption: IEEE Community in Greece
IEEEGreeceSection.text: The IEEE Greece Section is the national section of the IEEE in Greece. As part of IEEE Region 8, the Greece Section serves IEEE members across the country and contributes to the advancement of technology and engineering in Greece, as well as to the global IEEE community. The primary mission of the IEEE Greece Section is to support and advance the interests of electrical engineering, electronics, computer science, and related fields in Greece. The Section provides a platform for professional development, innovation, and networking for its members, as well as promoting educational activities. It fosters collaboration between academia, industry, and research organizations in Greece, facilitating the exchange of technical knowledge and ideas.

IEEERegion8.title: What is the IEEE Region 8?
IEEERegion8.caption: An IEEE Network – From Europe to Africa!
IEEERegion8.text: IEEE Region 8 is one of the 10 geographical regions of the IEEE, which is a global professional association for advancing technology. Region 8 includes Europe, the Middle East, and Africa (EMEA). The region encompasses a diverse range of countries and cultures, and it plays a vital role in the development and advancement of engineering, technology, and innovation across these areas.
